ember.note: Mirrored between themes so each step keeps its role, not its lightness. This ramp is the paper (default) order, darkest to lightest; the dark theme reverses it.

ember-deep.note: accent-300. The small-text tier and the only accent value that clears 4.5:1 on every surface in both themes — 6.77:1 on chalk ground, 7.49:1 on chalk surface, and as #f4a68c 10.00:1 and 9.28:1 on iron. Full-strength ember reaches only 3.51:1 on the chalk ground (measured 2026-08-14), so it is large-text and chrome only.

ember-ink.note: The near-black that sits on a filled ember surface.

chalk-ground.note: The default theme's page. Warm, not white.

chalk-surface.note: Cards and panels — the objects lying on the page.

chalk-hairline.note: A drawn border, for the rare case an edge will not do.

graphite.note: Text on chalk. Warm near-black, never pure black.

iron-ground.note: The dark theme's page. Warm as unlit iron — readable under gym lighting without flashing white mid-set.

display.purpose: The finish ceremony's total. One number, the whole screen.

input.purpose: Weight and reps. The thing the thumb is aiming at.

figure.purpose: Every other number a lifter reads. The floor for any figure.

title.purpose: Exercise names, screen headings, card titles.

kicker.purpose: The stamped label under an object. Mono, tracked, uppercase — and it drops to sans in Arabic, which has no case and whose joins tracking would break.

micro.purpose: Set counts, inline units. The smallest legible tier.

shadows.name: ring-hairline
shadows.purpose: The default elevation. A hairline ring plus a 1px inset light along the top edge — a milled surface catching room light, not an object floating over the page.

shadows.name: shadow-panel
shadows.purpose: The object you operate. Edge only, flush to the page.

shadows.name: shadow-card
shadows.purpose: The object you read from. Lifted one millimetre.

shadows.name: shadow-cta
shadows.purpose: The ember glow under the hero action. One per screen, or it is not a hero.

motion.name: motion-press
motion.purpose: The press dim. Answers: did my finger land?

motion.name: motion-instant
motion.purpose: A set row arriving. Answers: did my set save? Under the threshold where a person waits for it.

motion.name: motion-transition
motion.purpose: A layer sliding in. Answers: where did I come from?

motion.name: motion-celebration
motion.purpose: The record flash. Answers: did I beat it? Reachable only after the set is logged, never between one set and the next.

motion.name: motion-linear
motion.purpose: Used exactly once — the rest timer's drain, which is a readout of elapsed time rather than a response to a tap.

components.description: Solid ember, one per screen, on the single action that screen exists for.

components.name: Knurl Rule
components.description: The one texture in the system: cross-hatched ember at ±45°, 1px on a 5px period — the grip cut into a bar. Confined to thin bands, because knurling exists where a hand grips.
components.css: .ds-knurl-rule { --ds-knurl-ink: rgba(232, 73, 29, 0.7); width: 240px; height: 4px; border-radius: 999px; background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, var(--ds-knurl-ink) 0 1px, transparent 1px 5px), repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, var(--ds-knurl-ink) 0 1px, transparent 1px 5px); }

narrative.overview:
Loaded Ink is the conviction that a word can have mass — not describe mass, have it. The mark, the numerals and the surfaces are all treated the way a lifter treats iron: as objects with a centre of gravity and a load path. Everything either bears on the horizontal axis or hangs from it. Nothing floats, and nothing is decorative.

Two materials, and only two: chalk and iron. Chalk is the human trace — the off-white ground of the default paper theme, the written word, the hand. Iron is the machine — the warm near-black of the dark theme, and the single ember accent that is the material of the bar itself. The system ships both grounds from one token set: the same semantic names resolve to paper by default and to iron under [data-theme='dark'], and the ember ramp is mirrored between them so each step keeps its role rather than its lightness.

Density is the other half of the personality. This is a screen read at arm's length by someone with chalked hands, one thumb free, between sets, under whatever lighting the gym has. So the figures are enormous and tabular, the touch targets never go under 48px, and the chrome gets out of the way: no tab bar, no spinner on the hot path, no celebration screen. Motion is a plate landing, not a page turning — four durations in the whole app, two easings, and nothing on the logging path over 200ms.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds from one token set — paper by default, iron on request, never a third
One accent, ember #e8491d, and it is the only colour in the app
Numbers are the interface: Sora, tabular, never below 24px
Depth is an edge and a fill, not a drop shadow
One texture — the knurl — confined to thin bands and the PR badge
Logical properties only, because the Arabic flip is a planned flip, not a rewrite

rules.name: The Two Materials Rule
rules.body: Chalk and iron, plus ember. A third hue is not a design decision to be weighed; it is a defect. Charts, states, categories and muscle groups all express difference through the ember ramp or the neutral ramp, never through a second colour.

rules.name: The Mirrored Ramp Rule
rules.body: accent-100 through accent-900 swap ends between the two themes so that each step keeps its role: 300 is always "small accent text readable on this ground", 800–900 are always "tinted fill". Never reach for a step by its lightness; reach for it by its job.

rules.name: The 500-Is-Chrome Rule
rules.body: accent-500 on the ground is large text and chrome only. Small accent text uses accent-300. A 500-on-ground body-copy use is a contrast defect, not a taste question.

rules.name: The Runtime-Token Rule
rules.body: Tailwind v4 drops any @theme token nothing statically references, so a class name assembled at runtime compiles to nothing at all — no error, no warning, an empty element on screen. Accent steps used dynamically are declared as static classes. This has already caused two shipped defects.

rules.name: The Shadowed Scale Rule
rules.body: The radius tokens are declared in :root, not in @theme. Tailwind v4 still emits .rounded-lg { border-radius: var(--radius-lg) }, and the project's :root is parsed after Tailwind's — so the project value wins and rounded-lg really is 14px. That holds for sm/md/lg/xl only. 2xl is NOT overridden, so rounded-2xl falls back to Tailwind's 1rem — 16px, smaller than rounded-xl's 20px. The scale is non-monotonic above xl.

rules.name: The Ramp-Is-The-Target Rule
rules.body: The type scale is where new work goes, not a description of where the app is. Measured 2026-08-14: 189 literal text-[Npx] uses against 31 uses of the named steps. 135 of those are on-ramp values written the long way (11/13/15/19px) and are safe to convert on sight — converting them changes no pixels. The other 54, across 16 values, are genuinely off-ramp and mostly came from matching public/prototype.html. Do not round those onto the ramp; those pixels were chosen against a spec.

rules.name: The Figure Floor Rule
rules.body: No number a lifter reads goes below the figure tier (24px). The scale binds size, weight and leading together in one token so a size cannot be used at the wrong weight by accident.

rules.name: The Arabic Opt-Out Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono has no Arabic, and the platform monospace fallback draws Arabic as disconnected letters with gaps between them. Every mono class therefore has an RTL counterpart that drops to the sans stack and resets tracking and casing. Any new mono class that can hold a translated word needs the same escape hatch or it ships broken in Arabic.

rules.name: The Unlayered Voice Rule
rules.body: The Sora assignment rides on the size utilities themselves via an unlayered rule after the utilities layer, so no component names the family. Author CSS outside a layer outranks utilities — which is also why the native-control reset lists longhands and never `font: inherit` (the shorthand resets weight, and once pinned every button in the app to 400).

rules.name: The Named-Token Rule
rules.body: --surface-line is a real token in both themes because it was once written as var(--line), which the stylesheet never defined — and an undefined custom property invalidates the entire box-shadow declaration. Every panel in that release drew no edge at all, silently. A shadow composed from an undefined variable does not degrade; it vanishes.

rules.name: The One Ring Rule
rules.body: Rings are never stacked. A surface carries exactly one of the four named shadows.

rules.name: The Reduced-Motion Rule
rules.body: prefers-reduced-motion collapses the four duration tokens themselves and applies a global blanket, so an inline style that reads a token is stilled too. Every animation is both-filled, so collapsing the duration keeps the end state: a record row stays tinted, a committed set stays put.

dos: Do use logical properties exclusively — ms-, ps-, start-, text-start. ESLint fails the build on ml-, pl-, left-, text-left. The Arabic locale is a planned flip, not a rewrite.
Do give every accent step used dynamically a static class. A class name assembled at runtime compiles to no CSS and fails no check.
Do reach for accent-300 for any accent text under the figure tier, and accent-500 only for chrome and large text.
Do pair every mono utility with an [dir='rtl'] sans fallback if it can ever hold a translated word.
Do keep exactly one btn-hero per screen. Its authority comes entirely from being the only filled thing on the ground.
Do render numbers with .tnum, in Sora, at the figure tier or above.
Do state elevation with one of the four named shadow tokens.
donts: Don't introduce a second hue. Not for a chart series, not for a success state, not for a muscle group. The ember ramp and the neutral ramp carry every distinction this app needs to draw.
Don't compose a box-shadow from an undefined custom property. It does not degrade to a weaker shadow — the whole declaration is invalid and the edge vanishes silently.
Don't spread the knurl across a surface, or add it to something that already carries a shadow. One texture per surface, thin bands and the PR badge only.
Don't put a gradient anywhere except the header band, or a drop shadow anywhere except the four named tokens.
Don't use emoji, decorative illustration, or a celebration screen. A PR gets an ember flash on its own row.
Don't let anything on the logging path exceed 200ms, and don't put a spinner, modal or paywall on it at all.
Don't take an interactive touch target below 48px. (Display rows may be shorter — a logged set row is min-h-7. The floor governs things a thumb aims at.)
Don't reach for rounded-2xl or anything above it. Only sm/md/lg/xl are overridden, so 2xl silently falls back to Tailwind's 16px and renders tighter than xl.

Don't assume a component renders standalone. Most call useLocale, so they need LocaleProvider around them — without it they throw or render empty, which is how a component looks fine in the app and blank in a preview.
Don't write `font: inherit` on a native control; it silently resets weight and outranks the utility that asked for one.
Don't add a screen without a door to it on the home screen.
